position_start: Not held
position_end: A National Policy for ICT in Education sets goals for connectivity, ministry systems, staff training and school use of technology. The sector plan itself states that incorporating technology remains difficult for want of facilities, equipment and teacher training. Neither the policy nor the sector plan is held as a document, and the profile carrying them is a legacy platform its publisher states is no longer updated

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card and its issuance
position_start: Not held
position_end: Identity cards are issued by the Department of Immigration and Nationality, were first issued in 1992 and were handwritten until 2014. Applicants submit a supporting letter from their municipality administration, a birth certificate and proof of citizenship to one of twelve branch offices, which forward the application to headquarters in the capital for approval; a replacement costs 100 nakfa, the old card being surrendered and destroyed. The card carries name, sex, date and place of birth and an identification number in the two official languages. A newer electronic card carries a laser-engraved photograph, the holder's fingerprint and a unique serial number for tracing a lost card. Citizens aged 18 and over are required to hold one, and children of Eritrean parents may hold an underage card. No issuance volume, coverage rate or database behind the card is on record
note: The fullest account is a 2018 country-of-origin research response; the 2024 consular page confirms the requirement but adds no system detail

subject: dpi.pay
name: Banked population and the structure of the financial system
position_start: Not held
position_end: More than 70% of Eritreans are estimated to remain unbanked. The financial system is highly centralised on a small number of state-owned banks, one of which provides the majority of retail banking, which the account links to limited competition, minimal innovation and heavy reliance on manual processes. Mobile penetration was put at just under 60% of population in 2022, ranked 191st of 209 economies. The figures are a trade publication's estimates rather than a central bank or survey series, and no official financial inclusion measurement for the country is held

position_end: The country's return to the United Nations vital statistics questionnaire for reporting year 2025 leaves the completeness fields for birth and death registration blank, so no registration completeness estimate is reported at all.
